text: Once a sick bird is caught, a close examination can reveal diagnostic clinical signs. Head: comb and wattles should be red, bright, and waxy; eyes should be shiny, bright, and alert; nostrils should be clean with no discharge or breathing sounds. Breast: check whether it is full or skinny — a key indicator of insufficient feeding or chronic disease (though harder to assess in well-feathered layers) — and check for skin bruising. Vent: check for diarrhea signs and for visible parasites. Skin (body and legs): check for fighting injuries, stains, crusts, follicle damage, and parasites.
